thread:
pagerduty-bot: PAGERDUTY ALERT: P0 - GPU capacity exhaustion in prod-cluster-us-west-2. Paging oncall-infra and ops-lead. Incident started 2152468012

infra-bot: Kubernetes events: 5m ago - ScaleUp: ASG 'gpu-nodes-prod' reached max size (50)
infra-bot: Autoscaler log excerpt: "unable to scale up node group gpu-nodes-prod: LaunchTemplate version mismatch or insufficient IAM permissions"

sara: I'm on it, grabbing context. Queue growth metric looks scary on the generation queue. Customers seeing 429s and large tail latency.

dave: Report from monitoring: gen-queue length -> 18k waiting, token throughput decreased 4x. Some dedicated customers already routed to fallback but many on hosted tier impacted.

lisa: oncall-infra, can you confirm whether the autoscaler attempted to create nodes and got API errors?

oncall-infra: autoscaler attempted scale at 2152467940, 2152467985, error: 
```
Warning: Failed to launch instance: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation
Status Code: 403, Request ID: xxxxxxx
```
Looks like instance profile attach failed for the new LT version.

raj: That fits with yesterday's launch-template rollout. Ops changed instanceProfile from 'rwi-gpu-role-v1' -> 'rwi-gpu-role-v2' but the ASG/NodeGroup IAM role hasn't been granted by IAM team.

ops-lead: Confirming, we rolled a new launch template yesterday to pick up kernel/driver changes. It required a new instance profile. Policy grant is pending.

sara: Ok. Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert autoscaler to use previous LT version (if available) 2) increase ASG max temporarily and launch nodes with legacy LT manually 3) create a temporary nodegroup with correct instance profile and no taints 4) throttle gen-queue or route customers to Dedicated. Which is fastest?

dave: Manual nodegroup creation via eksctl/terraform could be fastest for a few extra nodes. Reverting LT might be quicker but risky if autoscaler picks wrong template.

oncall-infra: I'll try manual create with legacy launch template and attach the existing instance profile. Command I'm going to run: 
```
eksctl create nodegroup --cluster prod-cluster --name gpu-boost-temp --node-type p4d.24xlarge --nodes-min 0 --nodes-max 10 --node-labels role=gpu-temp --node-ami-family AmazonLinux2 --asg-access
```

infra-bot: Note: kubelet boot logs show pods stuck Pending due to taint: "gpu-reserved=true:NoSchedule" on current nodegroups; autoscaler won't place new pods until new nodes without taint available.

lisa: Can we remove the taint temporarily on existing nodegroups so some passengers can schedule? Need to be careful with isolation for dedicated customers.

raj: We should not remove taint on dedicated pools. But we can create a temporary untainted pool to absorb backlogged jobs. That keeps isolation.

ops-lead: @oncall-infra proceed with manual nodegroup creation, tag for non-dedicated usage. Also open an emergency request with IAM to grant instance profile attach permission to the LT.

oncall-infra: Running create now. ETA for node registration ~6-8 min. Will post kube events.

sara: Meanwhile, CS: please send a short note to impacted customers acknowledging we're mitigating and might see degraded throughput for ~15-30m. Keep it high level. @cs-rep take it.

cs-rep: Got it. Drafting message: "We're experiencing GPU provisioning delays which may affect generation latency and cause 429s. We're actively provisioning additional capacity; ETA ~20 min. We'll post updates here." Sending now.

infra-bot: New nodegroup bootstrap logs: 2152468209 - Instance i-0abcde registered, labels: role=gpu-temp, capacity: 8 GPUs

oncall-infra: Node registered, but kubelet shows kubelet error mounting nv driver. Running driver install script via userdata.

dave: If drivers fail, fallback plan: spin up p3xlarge with CPU-only fallback for lower-priority work, and prioritize critical customer traffic to Dedicated. 

lisa: Driver install succeeded on 3/4 nodes. One node still failing with kernel module mismatch. Mark it cordoned and continue with the 3 healthy ones.

infra-bot: Autoscaler status: "Scale up in progress: 3 nodes added from gpu-temp nodegroup. ASG gpu-nodes-prod still maxed at 50."

sara: Great. Start draining backlog: increase worker concurrency on newly registered nodes by bumping MUX config. Also enable prefix caching for repeat prompts to reduce immediate load.

oncall-infra: Patching deployment to prefer nodeSelector role=gpu-temp for hostpool-async. Patch applied.

raj: Also, we should throttle incoming requests from anonymous/unregistered customers by 50% at the API gateway to buy time. Can someone coordinate with edge?

ops-lead: I'll ask edge team now. Edge config change: set rate-limit rule for /v1/generate to 100req/s global for non-authenticated keys. Applying.

infra-bot: Edge change applied at 2152468271. Immediate drop in queue inflow ~40%.

cs-rep: Customers updated: message sent, some replies asking for SLA credits. Flagging for finance post-incident.

dave: Monitoring shows queue dropping from 18k -> 4.2k over 8 minutes. Tail latency improving. No new 500s.

lisa: Ops-Escalation: IAM team has been looped and expedited the instance profile grant. They say it's approved and propagating; once applied, we can update LT and allow autoscaler to use canonical LT again.

oncall-infra: Verified IAM change at 2152468319. I triggered a rollout: update nodegroup launch template to use v2 which includes new AMI/driver. Autoscaler will retry.

infra-bot: Autoscaler log: "ScaleUp: successfully launched 6 instances using LaunchTemplate v2"

sara: Once new nodes come ready, we'll migrate workloads back to managed nodegroups and decommission gpu-temp. Plan for rollback / cleanup: 1) drain and delete gpu-temp nodegroup 2) set ASG max back to previous 50 3) create postmortem with timeline and action items (LT rollout checklist, IAM pre-approve)

ops-lead: Agreed. Also add automated pre-flight check in CI to validate instance profile exists and IAM permissions are present for any LT changes.

cs-rep: Customer update: another note sent - "We have provisioned temporary capacity and are restoring throughput; you may see intermittent latency for up to 30 minutes."

dave: Queue is under 800 now. No active 429s in last 3m. Stability looks good.

lisa: thumbs up. Start cleanup when nodes idle. oncall-infra, coordinate the drain of gpu-temp and ensure no dedicated pods are scheduled on it before deletion.

oncall-infra: Starting cordon/drain sequence at 2152468348. Will remove nodegroup after pods evicted.

ops-lead: Incident status -> mitigated. We'll keep the channel open for 1 hour for follow-ups. Filing P0 incident doc and assigning postmortem to sara and raj.

sara: Postmortem focus: avoid live LT/IAM rollouts during traffic peaks, automated IAM validation, autoscaler guardrails for max-size ramp, and runbook for manual nodegroup creation.

pagerduty-bot: Incident closed to paging but channel remains. Acknowledged by oncall-infra. :white_check_mark: 

sara: Thanks team. Closing live mitigation. Full postmortem to follow. :thumbsup:
